reasons: Covers accepted, rejected and boundary cases for schedules, packages and attachments.
Uses the test runner named in the imports, so the checks can be run repeatedly.

terms.meaning: a tool that runs small automatic checks and reports which ones pass
the exact edge value of a limit, such as one byte over the maximum

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test tools and functions imported
sections.what: Brings in the test runner and the validation functions and limits that the tests check.
sections.why: Likely reason: the tests must use the same rules that the app uses.
sections.watch_out: If a function or limit is renamed, every test in this file will fail to load.

sections.name: visible schedule selection validation
sections.title: Schedule and attachment checks
sections.what: Checks that the supported schedule types are accepted, that unsupported types get a helpful explanation, that empty and oversized files are rejected, and that attachments are accepted within their limits.
sections.why: These are the everyday upload rules users hit most often.
sections.watch_out: Changing a size limit requires updating the boundary checks here as well.

sections.name: explicit project package selection
sections.title: Package and boundary checks
sections.what: Checks that only ZIP files are accepted as packages, that a ZIP is rejected as a schedule with a pointer to package mode, and that sizes at the exact limits are handled correctly.
sections.why: Keeps the two upload modes separate for users.
sections.watch_out: The package limit is checked against the attachment limit value, so changing that value changes these tests too.

summary: Automated checks that the upload rules accept the right files and reject the wrong ones, with the right explanation text.
purpose: Protects the upload rules and the wording shown to users from changing by accident.
why: Likely reason: the size limits and messages are things users rely on, so a change should be caught by a test.
how: Each test passes example file names and sizes to the validation functions and checks whether the result is valid, and whether the message contains the expected text.
inputs: Example file names and sizes, including the exact limit values.
outputs: A pass or fail result for each check, reported by the test runner.
risks: Some messages are checked with partial text, so a reworded message can still pass or can fail for an unrelated reason.
debug: If a test fails, compare the expected limit or file type with the matching value in the upload validation file, then check the message text.
